messages:
incident-bot: Pager: p99 latency spike detected for /v1/chat/stream in us-west-2 (SLO breach). Alert id: A-3987. Reason: tokenizer/preproc tail latency.

amanda: acked, taking lead. oncall here. seeing alerts showing p95 ~450ms -> p99 ~2.3s for streaming tails.

josh: noticed a surge in requests that include large tool_schema payloads and JSON-mode prompts starting ~10:12 UTC. concurrent streaming sessions + paging.

priya: adding context — we deployed prompt-template v2.3.1 at 09:58 that changed how tool schemas are inlined into prompt JSON. Might be inflating preproc work per request.

marco: logs show tokenizer CPU jitter on preproc-worker-7/8, lots of syscalls at parse_json_template() path. sample stack: 
```
parse_json_template -> expand_tool_schema -> tokenize_prefix -> kv_cache_lock
```

tina: rolling metrics: template expansion time per request median 28ms -> 310ms tail. KV cache miss rate up to 42% on these flows.

amanda: customer impact? cust-success, any support cases?

cust-success: 3 customers reported increased streaming stalls (UI reload) in last 30m. None are fully degraded but UX freeze for ~1-3s. High-value PLG accounts showing most.

josh: reproduction script attached (local):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream -d '{"model":"gptx-lite","prompt":"<template with tool_schema...>","mode":"json"}' --header 'Authorization: Bearer ...'
```
Hitting with parallel 200 threads reproduces the tail.

priya: hypothesis: inlining tool schemas into prompt JSON increases tokenization boundary complexity and triggers O(n^2) behavior for large schemas due to our naive template walker. Also JSON-mode adds extra validation passes.

marco: quick mitigation suggestions: 1) re-enable prefix/KV caching for template hashes, 2) throttle concurrent preproc workers for streaming endpoints, 3) roll back v2.3.1 if needed.

amanda: do we have a safe rollback?

josh: yes, we can rollback to v2.3.0 within the next 2 min. v2.3.1 is in the feature flag FG-TEMPLATE-INLINE. We can flip the flag to disable heavy inlining.

priya: flip done: FG-TEMPLATE-INLINE -> off. Confirming deploy change.

incident-bot: Feature flag FG-TEMPLATE-INLINE toggled off by josh at 10:27:14 UTC.

marco: monitoring... p99 dropping: 2.3s -> 980ms within 45s. p95 down to ~220ms. KV cache misses trending down.

amanda: good. still see a subset of streaming sessions with stalls ~800-1k ms. Looks like some long-running cached eviction cascades.

marco: I'll add an emergency cache warmup for top templates to decrease cold-start churn. Pushing a small job to prefill prefix cache on preproc-workers.

josh: also temporarily bumping preproc worker count by +2 on us-west-2 autoscaling group. scaling action executed.

priya: note: a correlated commit earlier also increased strict JSON validation when mode==json. We can relax strict schema validation to a softer pass while we investigate. That reduces CPU by ~12% in canary.

amanda: do it. priya, proceed with soft-validate on json-mode for production.

priya: soft-validate rollout queued and applied to 30% of traffic at 10:31.

marco: p99 now ~550ms, p95 ~180ms. streaming stall count down 87% from peak.

cust-success: relaying to affected customers that we are mitigating, ETA for full resolution ~20-30m. they appreciate the note.

amanda: we should keep page open for on-call handoff. leaving for josh for deeper root cause and postmortem. I'll handoff ops.

josh: taking over. I'll collect traces, flamegraphs, and diff between 2.3.0 and 2.3.1 template walker. Also capture requests that hit >1s tail.

incident-bot: Oncall handoff requested by amanda to josh at 10:36:08 UTC.

josh: quick notes: suspect function expand_tool_schema() is doing repeated string concatenations and re-parsing when tool_schema contains nested arrays. That combined with JSON-mode validation loops is expensive. We'll gather flamegraphs.

priya: I have a local patch to memoize expanded schemas per request template hash. If safe, we can land a hotfix to avoid re-walking same tool schema per tokenization pass.

marco: can we QA the memoize patch on a single preproc-worker?

priya: yes, deploying canary to preproc-worker-3 now.

amanda: timeline: initial alert 10:12, FF flip 10:27, soft-validate 10:31, p99 improved 10:33. Next steps: canary patch, postmortem, customer follow-up.

josh: canary results: request tail samples dropped 65% on canary worker. patch looks promising. I'll prepare a rollback-safe hotfix and run it through canary after a quick code review.

cust-success: customers updated. one asked for a root cause summary after incident.

amanda: logging note: need to add a new metric 'template_inline_elapsed_ms' and tag by 'tool_schema_size' and 'json_mode' so we can alert earlier next time.

marco: adding dashboard tile and alert: trigger if template_inline_elapsed_ms p99 > 600ms for >5m.

josh: preparing postmortem draft. I'll include timeline, mitigations, code diffs, and follow-ups: memoize expanded schemas, limit inlining size, safer defaults for FG-TEMPLATE-INLINE, improve tests for nested tool_schema, and add alert.

priya: I'll file the PR for hotfix with feature branch name: hotfix/template-memoize-3987. Requesting fast review from eng-runtime.

amanda: thanks everyone. leaving final notes: severity SEV3 (user-visible slowdowns), customer impact moderate, mitigated by FF flip + soft validation + cache warmup. Handing to josh for postmortem and closure.

josh: capturing final action items in incident board. Closing active page in 30m if no regression.

incident-bot: Incident A-3987 marked 'mitigated' by josh at 10:58:21 UTC.

marco: quick follow-up: please keep tracing for next 24h and share any spike tags.

amanda: copy. I'll update oncall notes and add to rotation briefing.

cust-success: will follow up with customers with incident summary and link to postmortem when available.

josh: closing thread after 30m monitoring window if stable.
